response:
Diagnosis. The worst-of-dangers structure is the clear winner of gen 7: WorstDangerShortfallOrBrokenProfit delivered the archive's best cross-sectional slope (fmb -4.98) together with a large reliable alpha (-4.4%, t -4.46) at high coverage (0.140), improving the shortfall's slope from -2.78 while retaining most of its alpha. Two further lessons: (i) monotone extremum/level constructions dominate rank-times-z products — RevenueContractionWithLiquidityBuffer got alpha +4.0% (t 3.63) with a *wrong-signed* slope (-1.61), and SupplierCreditStretchWithoutCashCover got alpha -2.8% with a null slope (0.75), both classic symptoms of the non-negative-rank product; (ii) the capacity-adjusted profit measure (gross profit minus depreciation) has been the strongest quality leg wherever it appears. This batch consolidates on the danger-extremum family, repairs the two misaligned products into monotone forms, and asks two sharply posed leg-definition questions (current versus scarred distress, level versus downside quality).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: TripleDangerFinancingProfitDecline
EXPRESSION: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), MAX(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(GROWTH(revt, 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms fail through three separable routes — a maturity wall that internal funds cannot cover, operations that do not earn a surplus after replacing consumed capacity, and a shrinking revenue base that invalidates the existing cost structure — and because none of these is rescued by strength elsewhere, expected returns are set by whichever danger is largest.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two-danger version produced the archive's best joint evidence, and the natural next question is whether an operating-decline channel that shares no inputs with either existing leg tightens the identification of endangered firms or merely dilutes it. Revenue contraction has shown independent portfolio power (alpha +4.0% in the conditional form) but a broken slope, so putting it on the common danger z-scale is also the monotone repair that its own specification needed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ScarDangerMax
EXPRESSION: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 5), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Credit terms are set by a firm's worst recent refinancing position rather than its current one, so the danger that binds is the peak five-year funding shortfall paired with the current failure to earn a capacity-adjusted surplus; a firm that has been to the wall remains rationed even after the gap closes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The peak shortfall was a stronger cross-sectional predictor than the current level (fmb -3.43 versus -2.78) with a comparable alpha, so substituting it inside the winning worst-of structure isolates a single well-posed question: is the danger a current state or an accumulated scar. This is a leg-definition test within the best-performing operator, not a horizon variant of a standalone signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: OperatingDeclineOrIlliquidityDanger
EXPRESSION: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(GROWTH(revt, 1))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(che, lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: A contracting top line and a thin cash buffer are separate hazards: a shrinking firm with cash restructures on its own schedule and a liquid firm with growing revenue is safe, but a firm exposed on either dimension faces forced action, so the worse of the two governs expected returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The conditional form of this pair produced a solid alpha with a wrong-signed slope, which the archive has repeatedly shown to be the signature of a non-negative rank multiplying a centered conditioner; expressing both hazards on a common industry-z danger scale and taking the maximum keeps the economics while restoring monotonicity. It also tests the danger-extremum operator on a pair that contains no balance-sheet funding-gap variable, telling us whether the operator or the shortfall channel is doing the work.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: CapacityAdjustedWeakestLinkSolvency
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The survival-relevant measure of operating strength is profit after the cost of replacing consumed capacity, not gross profit: a firm whose gross margin is entirely absorbed by depreciation cannot fund claims from operations, so the binding-constraint pairing of liquidity with capacity-adjusted profitability should price distress better than the gross-profit version.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's best safety signal pairs liquidity with gross profitability (alpha +4.7%, t 4.03), and capacity-adjusted profit has been the stronger quality leg in every conditional test where both appeared (fmb 4.26), so this asks whether depreciation belongs in the survival measure — a substantive accounting-economics question rather than a scaling tweak. It is the natural safety-side counterpart to the danger-side legs used above, keeping the batch internally comparable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: NetSupplierFinancingGap
EXPRESSION: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lct, dlc), che), cogs), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Payables and accruals net of cash, expressed in years of operating cost, measure how much of the firm's operations are financed by suppliers who can withdraw terms at will; a large net supplier financing gap is a fragile, on-demand liability structure that predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The conditional version of this new trade-credit channel produced a reliable alpha (-2.8%, t -2.67) but no cross-sectional slope, and the monotone repair — netting cash inside the measure rather than multiplying by a cash conditioner — should deliver both, exactly as the same repair did for the funding shortfall in gen 5. Scaling by cost of goods keeps the measure an operating-cycle duration rather than a balance-sheet ratio, and the denominator is strictly positive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: DownsideProfitDangerMax
EXPRESSION: MAX(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: What makes a funding gap lethal is not average profitability but the firm's demonstrated downside: if its capacity-adjusted profit has fallen to or below zero at some point in the last five years, lenders know the firm can stop covering its own capital consumption, so the worse of current financing pressure and worst-case operating surplus should price distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The floor concept has independently produced reliable alphas in this archive (DemonstratedCoverageFloor +3.5%, t 3.17), and pairing a downside quality leg with the current funding danger asks whether the interaction operates through realized downside rather than the current level — the mirror of the question asked in Signal 2 on the distress side. Together the two signals decompose which side of the interaction carries the historical information.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE TripleDangerFinancingProfitDecline---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The two-leg MAX is already the archive's best signal and the archive's own TripleWeakestLink experiment showed that adding a third leg dilutes rather than sharpens, while the new revenue-contraction leg carries a sign that both its own archived conditional test (fmb -1.61 against a positive prior) and the documented sales-growth/value effect (low past sales growth earns *higher* returns) argue against treating as a danger.

---CRITIQUE ScarDangerMax---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical MAX of two already-evaluated archive signals (PeakHistoricalFundingShortfall and the capacity-adjusted profit leg of WorstDangerShortfallOrBrokenProfit) whose legs are near-collinear with the current-level version, so the result is largely predetermined and unlikely to yield information beyond what the two components have already delivered.

---CRITIQUE OperatingDeclineOrIlliquidityDanger---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Both legs are weak: cash-to-current-liabilities in the "low cash predicts low returns" direction is essentially the published cash-holdings anomaly, and the revenue-contraction leg has already failed cross-sectionally in this archive and points against the sales-growth literature, so the MAX operator is being tested on a pair with no credible prior on either component.

---CRITIQUE CapacityAdjustedWeakestLinkSolvency---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Replacing gross-profit-to-assets with the same quantity net of depreciation inside the archive's already-evaluated WeakestLinkSolvency is a substitution of a highly correlated leg, so this is closer to a cosmetic re-specification of the incumbent winner than the substantively different improvement the objective calls for.

---CRITIQUE NetSupplierFinancingGap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: A genuinely distinct trade-credit-duration channel with a monotone, well-scaled, strictly-positive-denominator construction and a clear ex-ante motivation from the failed conditional version, though the reviewer should verify the result is not simply the cash-holdings effect re-entering through the netted che term.

---CRITIQUE DownsideProfitDangerMax---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The realized-downside profitability leg is a new construct rather than a repackaged archive signal, making this the more informative of the batch's MAX-leg experiments, but the five-year minimum of capacity-adjusted profit is likely highly correlated with its level, so a small delta versus WorstDangerShortfallOrBrokenProfit should be interpreted as no evidence for the downside mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: MaturityMismatchAgainstAssetLife
EXPRESSION: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), dp), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Runs are caused by funding long-lived assets with on-demand money: net short-term debt expressed in units of annual capital consumption measures how many years of the asset base are financed by claims that can be withdrawn within twelve months, and firms with a severe mismatch are repriced downward when credit conditions tighten.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is a maturity-structure-versus-asset-life mismatch, not a coverage or profitability measure — depreciation enters as the inverse of asset longevity rather than as a charge against income — so it is economically distinct from every shortfall and coverage specification in the archive, none of which uses asset life. It is monotone over a strictly positive denominator for operating firms, which is the specification property that has consistently produced aligned slope and alpha in this archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AbnormalRefinancingPressure
EXPRESSION: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), MA(RATIO(SUB(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), at), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms differ permanently in how much short-term funding their business model requires, so what signals trouble is refinancing pressure above the firm's own normal level; a distributor that always runs a gap is not distressed, whereas a firm whose gap has moved well above its own five-year norm is.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This changes the normalization axis rather than the horizon: the cross-sectional level, its one-year change, and its five-year peak have all been tested, but never the deviation from the firm's own recent norm, and the within-firm axis produced the archive's strongest slope elsewhere (fmb 4.87). It should also fix the specific failure of the one-year change specification, which had a powerful slope but no alpha because single-year swings reverse, whereas a deviation from a five-year mean is a persistent state.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: OperatingCycleHoleInYearsOfProfit
EXPRESSION: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(wcap), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: A working-capital deficit is a hole that must be filled out of operating earnings, and the economically meaningful measure is how long that takes: the deficit divided by normalized gross profit gives the years of production required to close it, and firms needing many years of output to cover their operating-cycle shortfall are the ones suppliers and short-term lenders ration.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The working-capital-deficit axis has only ever been used as a non-negative conditioning rank in this archive, where it produced a strong slope but a modest alpha, and expressing it instead as a monotone quality-scaled duration is the same repair that turned the rollover quotient into the archive's best portfolio signal. Normalizing by three-year average gross profit rather than assets removes firm size from the measure and makes the distress dimension explicitly relative to earning capacity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: StockVersusFlowSolvencyWeakestLink
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs)), lct), at), 5), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Solvency requires both an accumulated record of having funded its own claims over the cycle and current earning power after replacing consumed capacity; a firm with a strong five-year record but no current surplus is in decline, and one with a good current surplus but no accumulated record has never been tested, so the weaker of the two binds.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Unlike swapping a highly correlated leg into the incumbent minimum, this pairs channels at genuinely different horizons — a five-year cumulative resource stock and a current-year capacity-adjusted flow — each of which delivered independently reliable alphas (+3.7% t 3.32 and +2.6% t 3.00) from different information. The horizon complementarity is the economic claim being tested: demonstrated history and current earning power are not substitutes for survival.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
